newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth CEO sees AT&T tactics.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth CEO sees AT&T tactics.

text.p: BellSouth Corp Chief Executive Duane Ackerman on Thursday accused AT&T Corp of intentionally being slow to enter the local residential market in the U.S. South in order to keep BellSouth out of long-distance.

In remarks prepared for a speech to business leaders, Ackerman said AT&T and other "competitors" had told regulators that BellSouth should not be allowed into the long-distance market because of the lack of competition in local residential markets within its service region.
He said the long-distance giant had chosen to concentrate on local service for high-end business customers rather than enter the residential market.
"The upshot is that AT&T has every financial incentive not to move into local residential service in a big way," he told the Atlanta Chamber of Commerce.
"The slower they go, the longer they believe they can delay our entry into long distance. The slower they go, the more of our business they believe that they can take."
